# How to Summarize a 30-Page Work Report into 5 Key Points with ChatRTX

> **In short:** ChatRTX is a free NVIDIA app that runs on your own Windows PC and answers questions about files in a folder you choose. You can ask it for five key points from a long PDF. It needs a Windows computer with a compatible NVIDIA RTX graphics card, and it cannot replace reading the report.

Long reports pile up, and the meeting starts in an hour. By the end of this guide, you'll have ChatRTX read a long PDF on your own computer and give you five key points to scan before the meeting. This is written for anyone who uses a Windows work laptop or desktop and wants a quick overview of a document without reading every page first.

## Before you start
- **A Windows PC with an NVIDIA RTX graphics card.** ChatRTX does not run on Macs, phones or computers without this kind of card. To check, press the Windows key, type "Device Manager," and open **Display adapters**. If you see a name with "RTX" in it, you're set.
- **Free disk space and patience.** The app and its AI files are large (several gigabytes), so make sure you have plenty of room. The download can take a while.
- **Your PDF, saved on your computer.** Plan on about 20 minutes total, most of it waiting for the download.
- **Permission to install software.** If your work computer is managed by your company's IT team, you may not be allowed to install apps. Ask before you begin.

## Step 1 — Find the official ChatRTX download page
Open your web browser and search for "NVIDIA ChatRTX." Choose the result that leads to NVIDIA's own website. Look for a download button or a link that says something like "Download" or "Get ChatRTX." Avoid third-party download sites, since you want the official installer. NVIDIA describes ChatRTX as a free demo app, and the exact wording and page layout may change, so read the page carefully before you click.

The page will also list system requirements. If your graphics card or Windows version doesn't match, the app won't run, so check that list first. Save the installer file to your Downloads folder.

You'll know it worked when you have an installer file on your computer and you've confirmed it came from NVIDIA's website.

## Step 2 — Install ChatRTX and open it
Double-click the installer and follow the on-screen steps. Windows may ask whether you trust the app. Click **Yes** only if the file came from NVIDIA's site. The installer will usually ask where to place the app and may download large AI files along the way. Leave the computer on until it finishes.

When it's done, look for a new ChatRTX icon on your desktop or in the Start menu. Open it. The app usually opens in your web browser as a page with a chat box. If it looks different, that's fine: versions vary, and some launch in a small window instead.

You'll know it worked when the ChatRTX window or browser page opens and shows a place to type a message.

## Step 3 — Point ChatRTX at your report
ChatRTX answers questions about files you put in a folder it can read. Create a new folder on your computer, such as "Work Reports," and move your PDF into it. Keep only the documents you want the app to read, so the answers stay focused.

Inside ChatRTX, look for a tab or option with a name like **Dataset** or **Your files**. It lets you choose a folder. Select the folder you just made, then look for a button like **Create dataset** or **Build** and click it. The app will process the files, which can take a few minutes for a 30-page document. If the processing never finishes, the file may be a scanned image without real text. Use a digital PDF instead.

You'll know it worked when the app confirms the dataset is ready or shows your PDF's name in the list.

## Step 4 — Ask for five key points
Go back to the main chat box, and make sure your dataset is selected if the app gives you a choice. Type your request, and fill in the square-bracket parts with your own details. Press Enter or the send button.

💬 Example: "Summarize the report [report name] into 5 key points for a busy [job title]. Keep each point to two sentences, and note the page number where each point appears."

It usually takes a short while for the answer to appear, and the text may fill in gradually. If the answer is too general, ask again with more detail, such as "Focus only on costs and deadlines." If it misses the point, that's normal. Rephrase with specifics and try again.

You'll know it worked when you see a numbered list of five points that matches the report's topic.

## Step 5 — Check the summary against the report
Before you rely on the summary, open the original PDF and check two or three points. Use the page numbers ChatRTX gives you, or search the PDF for key words. AI tools can misread tables, charts and numbers, and they can miss things. ChatRTX can help you prepare, but it cannot promise a complete or perfectly accurate summary.

If a point looks wrong, ask a follow-up question in the same chat, such as "Where in the report does it say the budget increased?" Then confirm the answer in the document yourself.

💬 Example: "Quote the sentence that supports point 3, and tell me which page it is on."

You'll know it worked when the points you checked match the text of the original report.

## Common mistakes
- **Trusting the summary without checking it.** The fix is to verify any number, date or decision against the original before you repeat it in a meeting.
- **Loading too many files at once.** A dataset full of unrelated documents can blur the answers. The fix is to keep one report, or a small set of related ones, in each folder.
- **Uploading confidential material without checking the rules.** NVIDIA describes ChatRTX as running on your own computer, but your company may still have policies about sensitive data. The fix is to ask your manager or IT team before loading private documents.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** Use it on a long document you have to understand, such as a lease summary you're reviewing for personal reasons. Keep in mind it can't give legal or financial advice, so read the real document yourself.
- **For your business or work:** Turn a long weekly report into five bullet points before a status meeting. You still read the key pages, but you walk in prepared.
- **If you're just getting started:** Start with a short, non-sensitive document, like a company newsletter or a public report, so you can learn the steps without any risk.

## Try it now
Find a PDF you already have on your computer that's about ten pages or more. Ask yourself what you need from it, then write one sentence describing it. Use that sentence to ask ChatRTX for three key points once the app is installed. If you're not ready to install yet, check the NVIDIA page for system requirements first. That alone tells you whether this tool fits your computer.
